records.title: React DOM renderer requires a compatible React peer
records.summary: A React DOM 18.3.1 renderer paired with React 18.2.0 fails a strict npm peer-resolution check. In the pinned fixture, upgrading both React and React DOM to 18.3.1 passes the same installation check. This is evidence for the tested pair, not a universal version guarantee.
conditions: The project declares react-dom and react versions whose peer requirements must be reconciled.
The authorized scope permits checking or aligning the React renderer and the React package together.
actions: Read the actual react-dom target peerDependencies from the approved registry before changing declarations.
If the current React provider violates that peer range, propose an in-scope compatible React version; never silently change held declarations.
Run the receiving project's frozen install, renderer tests, and runtime acceptance on its final tree.
verification: Run a strict npm peer-resolution check against the exact approved versions.
Inspect the effective installed react/react-dom pair using npm ls.
Run the recipient project's React renderer and server-rendering tests.

actions: For the tested pair, set esbuild.jsx to transform while preserving the existing factory and fragment. Vite 8 deprecates this compatibility option.
Use explicit Oxc classic JSX settings only after the supported host range permits them. Verify peer ranges and receiving project behavior.
conditions: The Vite config sets esbuild.jsxFactory and jsxFragment to the non-React Html factory and Fragment without selecting a JSX runtime.
The receiving project uses classic JSX and verifies the exact transition from Vite 7.3.6 to 8.1.5.
records.summary: The classic Html factory and fragment settings in Fastify HTMX 0.4.1 work with Vite 7.3.6. With Vite 8.1.5, the original settings select a React JSX runtime. Explicitly selecting the classic transform restores the expected HTML on both tested versions.
records.title: Preserve classic JSX for Fastify HTMX on Vite 8.1.5
verification: Use a frozen install and build a representative JSX entry. Assert the emitted code renders the expected HTML.
Run the same control on every supported host Vite line before changing a reusable plugin.

records.title: Check generated Prisma enum values when moving to 7.0.0
records.summary: The pinned fixture emits mapped database values for UserPermissionRole on Prisma 7.0.0. Prisma 6.19.0 and 7.3.0 emit the schema member names. This finding applies to the tested generator versions.
conditions: The evaluated transition is @prisma/client 6.19.0 to 7.0.0 with the Prisma CLI at the same exact version.
The PostgreSQL schema has @map on enum members and application code observes or serializes the generated enum values.
actions: Check the exact CLI and client pins, then regenerate Prisma Client on a frozen lockfile.
Compare emitted values with application comparisons, fixtures, API responses and persisted database values before changing callers.
Test the actual selected Prisma patch. The 7.3.0 control restored the same generated values as 6.19.0.
verification: Check generated values using the recipient schema and exact CLI/client versions.
Test database round trips and the external representation of enum values in the receiving application when it exposes them.

actions: Keep the React runtime and renderer pair aligned. Reproduce the immediate read on the selected pair before changing the benchmark.
If the selected legacy fixture returns null before commit, wait for a bounded initial commit signal before starting benchmark timing. Fail when the expected static tree never commits.
conditions: The benchmark consumes toJSON() immediately after create() for a static host tree using the deprecated React Test Renderer.
The verified transition pairs React and react-test-renderer at 18.3.1 before the change and 19.3.0 after it. Reproduce the timing independently on any other pair.
Check that the benchmark measures serialization and permits waiting for fixture setup before timing starts.
records.summary: For the static legacy host-tree benchmark pattern, immediate toJSON() on the matched React and renderer 19.3.0 pair returned null in development and production. A bounded initial commit signal preserved the expected static JSON in both modes. The 18.3.1 pair returned that tree synchronously.
records.title: Read React Test Renderer JSON after the initial commit
verification: Freeze dependencies and verify the installed React and renderer versions.
Compare the exact static host tree with the React 18.3.1 synchronous control in development and production. Check that the benchmark still serializes the same fixture outside setup timing.
Run the receiving benchmark and compatibility tests.

actions: Run the Tailwind v4 CLI with --optimize when generating the CSS consumed by next build.
Regenerate the stylesheet in the build lifecycle when it is a precompiled app import.
conditions: Next.js is exactly 13.4.6 and its production CssMinimizerPlugin processes generated CSS.
The npm migration is Tailwind 3.3.2 to 4.0.0 with CLI, node and oxide all 4.0.0.
The generated stylesheet contains nested responsive rules such as lg:flex and lg:hidden. The evidence is scoped to their CSS behavior.
records.summary: Next 13.4.6 can merge nested responsive selectors that share a media query and lose distinct display declarations. On the checked npm transition, Tailwind 4.0.0 CLI --optimize flattens the selectors before Next minifies the CSS and restores desktop menu visibility.
records.title: Flatten Tailwind 4 responsive CSS before Next 13.4.6 production minification
verification: Inspect the real production CSS, then verify mobile hidden, desktop visible, and desktop hidden controls.
Retain the caller’s browser and runtime gates. A successful build alone does not detect this issue.

actions: Install the matching @tailwindcss/postcss adapter and use the Tailwind CSS import. Explicitly load any retained JS configuration.
Where the original default small shadow must remain, use shadow-xs and compare actual rendered shadow geometry. Verify custom radius independently.
Use outline-hidden where retaining the v3 forced-colors outline is required. Verify keyboard focus in the receiving application.
conditions: The npm project moves from Tailwind 3.4.4 to 4.3.3 and directly uses Tailwind as a PostCSS plugin.
Default utility names are present in rendered controls. Compare custom theme values before applying any codemod.
The checked compiler uses @tailwindcss/postcss 4.3.3 and PostCSS 8.5.33; the v3 control uses PostCSS 8.4.38.
records.summary: Tailwind 4.3.3 rejects the v3 direct PostCSS plugin. After changing adapter and CSS entry, held shadow-sm compiles with different geometry. Select shadow-xs for the verified default shadow. For a custom rounded-sm, preserve the configured radius and verify its emitted value.
records.title: Check emitted styles after switching Tailwind to its v4 PostCSS adapter
verification: Use frozen installs and verify the compiler versions and applicable browser targets.
Inspect built CSS for shadow geometry, the configured radius and the forced-colors selector. Compare the receiving application in relevant browsers and themes.

actions: Check the declaration worker and its effective compiler options in addition to the top-level tsc version.
For a bundled ESM leaf with no aliases, check bundler module resolution and remove the empty baseUrl and paths configuration.
If tsup still injects an unused baseUrl, test a pinned pnpm patch that removes only the implicit fallback. Review other tsup users before adopting it across a workspace.
conditions: The source specifically upgrades TypeScript 5.9.2 to 6.0.3 with tsup 8.5.0 held and declarations enabled under pnpm.
The leaf emits through a bundler, legacy aliases are absent, and the actual tsup DTS worker uses TypeScript 6.0.3.
records.summary: tsup 8.5.0 inserts baseUrl into its declaration compiler options. On TypeScript 6.0.3 this can cause TS5101 even after a leaf tsconfig removes baseUrl and changes module resolution to bundler.
records.title: Check tsup’s implicit baseUrl when TypeScript 6 declaration builds fail
verification: Frozen install the exact graph. Run tsup through declaration emission; a JavaScript-only success or passing Vitest run leaves DTS unverified.
Exercise ESM and CJS entry points and declaration consumers with the receiving project’s export map, recording baseline failures.
Compare generated JavaScript and declarations against a clean baseline and verify downstream typecheck.

actions: Set build.lib.cssFileName to the basename used by the existing public stylesheet contract.
Check package exports and consumers that reference the file by name.
conditions: The receiving package uses Vite library mode, emits a stylesheet, and exposes or otherwise relies on its filename.
The exact verified transition is Vite 5.4.2 to 8.3.8 with the same source CSS.
records.summary: With build.lib enabled and a package name of probe-library, Vite 5.4.2 writes style.css and Vite 8.3.8 writes probe-library.css. An explicit build.lib.cssFileName value of style restores style.css on 8.3.8.
records.title: Preserve a published Vite library stylesheet filename
verification: Use npm ci with a pinned lockfile and run both library builds.
Assert the emitted name and CSS contents, then check downstream imports if the receiving project exports the stylesheet.

actions: Convert the object mapping to build.rolldownOptions.output.codeSplitting.groups.
Match the actual resolved Vue runtime module IDs and give their group a higher priority when dependencies compete for ownership.
Keep independent controls for successful typecheck and correct runtime module placement.
conditions: The project moves from Vite 7.3.6 to 8.3.8 and uses an explicit object-form build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks configuration.
The intended chunk topology groups Vue runtime code with Vue Router and Pinia and separates the UI library. Check the receiving project's emitted graph and peer versions.
records.summary: With the same Vue plugin 6.0.7, Vite 8.3.8 rejects the object-form manualChunks accepted by Vite 7.3.6. A name-only Rolldown port can still build while moving @vue/runtime-dom outside the intended Vue chunk.
records.title: Replace object-form manualChunks and verify Vue runtime placement
verification: Use a frozen dependency installation with compatible Vite plugin and Vue versions.
Run typecheck and production build. Inspect module membership and chunk import links in the emitted output.
Exercise the receiving app's lazy routes and UI interactions.

actions: Read the chosen Vitest version peerDependencies and match the exact Vite version before updating declarations.
If the Vite version is held outside the asserted peer range, report the conflict. Otherwise choose a compatible Vite version and check every Vite plugin peer range.
Check Vitest-specific typing and setup imports, then run the receiving project build and tests.
conditions: The current graph contains Vitest 2.1.2 with Vite 5.4.8 and the selected Vitest target is 5.0.0.
The environment satisfies the exact target Node.js engines and uses npm 11.16.0 for the reproduced resolver check. The authorized scope allows changes to Vite and affected plugins.
records.summary: In a strict npm fixture, Vitest 5.0.0 rejects held Vite 5.4.8 with ERESOLVE. Vitest 5.0.0 with Vite 6.4.0 passes the same check and installs with the generated lock unchanged.
records.title: Vitest 5 requires a compatible Vite peer
verification: Use strict npm peer resolution and compare installed Vite and Vitest versions with the intended pair.
Run npm ci and verify the lock remains unchanged.
Run the receiving project build, typecheck and runtime tests.

actions: Use module scope for calls that should be hoisted.
For dynamic mocking, use vi.doMock or vi.doUnmock with a later dynamic import and verify the ordering for the test.
conditions: The receiving Node runner is moving from Vitest 4.1.10 to 5.0.0 and contains vi.mock, vi.unmock or vi.hoisted below module scope.
The worked fixture uses npm and resolves Vite 7.3.6 on both sides.
records.summary: Vitest 4.1.10 warns for nested vi.mock, vi.unmock and vi.hoisted. Vitest 5.0.0 rejects their test modules during the mock transform, before any test runs.
records.title: Move hoisted Vitest mocking calls to module scope
verification: Install both graphs from frozen npm lockfiles.
Require each nested API to fail before tests in the Vitest 5 runner. Check a valid top-level version and a dynamic mocking case in both runners.
